speaker: new_mother
quote: If one more person tells me to sleep when the baby sleeps, I will lose whatever marbles I have left. It’s not that easy.
context: Four weeks after the birth, sleeping on the couch with a baby who only sleeps held.

speaker: new_mother
quote: He sleeps in our bed alone at night so that he can be somewhat rested for work. Idk what to do when I have to go back to work as well if this is still like this.
context: She does all nights so her husband can work.

speaker: new_mother
quote: there’s advice here telling  me to do the contact naps during the day for better night sleep, and telling me to transfer to the bassinet during the day for better night sleep lol.
context: Reading the replies to her post.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’ve been waking up every morning completely overwhelmed, giant to do list that only grows, feeling defeated and like I’ll never get it done in time.
context: Third trimester, preparing alone.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: he keeps telling me to “tell him what to do to help and he’ll do it” but that’s not the point. I thought we were equally in this together and now I’m feeling really stupid realizing, no actually, we’re not.
context: Her husband waits for instructions while she carries the preparation.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: he gets to suddenly realize at the hospital “omg this is real!” while I’ve been doing everything else, the entire pregnancy and all the prep. this all makes me extremely nervous for post partum
context: Why the preparation gap makes her dread the weeks after the birth.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I’m due in 4 weeks and have an 18 month old and I’ve hit a breaking point between the exhaustion of being pregnant and taking care of a toddler.
context: Asking mothers of two under two if it gets better.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I live in a rural area, 45 minutes from the hospital and am having some fear my upcoming birth might be too fast. Can anyone provide any insight or similar experiences to help me prepare?
context: After a first labour of about six hours, asking what to expect the second time.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I have the 34 week consultant appointment tomorrow where consent forms are signed, but wanted to check if there’s anything else that would be discussed or done at this appointment and what to expect?
context: UK, planned surgical birth for personal reasons.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I feel like I should be more "prepared" than I am because I've done this before, but I'm worried that it'll be so different and much harder.
context: Due any day with her second, after a first birth that skipped most stages of labour.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: We had the idea of going on a cruise for a babymoon the 3rd week in July but found out that they won’t let me go on because I’d be too pregnant!
context: Utah, planning a July babymoon at seven months.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I LOVE the idea of endless shops to visit, historical tours, walkable cities, and not spending 8,000 dollars to do it all.
context: Her babymoon wish list after the cruise fell through.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: It stays with me about for about 3 hours after I wake up. That leaves me dealing with it at work for a whole hour, which is not great when I do a lot of walking.
context: 9 weeks, morning nausea that only eases lying down.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: My mom will get him a couple days a week and will do things with him, and when my husband comes home he plays with him until he goes to bed, but I can’t help but feel like a terrible mom.
context: 32 weeks with her second, too exhausted to play with her 2.5-year-old.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: The state I live in doesn’t offer paid maternity leave so I’m trying to wait until last minute possible so that I have a source of income since I’m not done buying baby stuff but I am absolutely fcking exhausted.
context: US, 32 weeks, her fiancé earns little as a server.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I just wish so bad I could go on leave because my soul is tired at this point and my body hurts so so bad
context: 32 weeks, working on with no paid leave.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: People have reached out to me essentially calling dibs on items while telling me they are going to wait to purchase it. And I'm like I'm not reserving this item for you?
context: 20 weeks, first registry, posted after the anatomy scan.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I added links to the registries (babylist and target) and explained why there were two (taking advantage of free gift boxes)
context: Two registries for the free welcome boxes; she asked for clean second-hand items too.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: My grandma also insulted the crib I had put on the registry saying it was too expensive
context: A convertible wooden crib on her registry.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: My real goal is to spend as little money as possible on necessities before the baby arrives.
context: Why her registry invites second-hand gifts.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: like 3 people have just said they'll buy a crib. I don't need 3 cribs. I need 1 crib, but I also would like a stroller, car seat, diapers, etc.
context: Family promising the same item instead of following the registry.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Not sure how to proceed from here, and if I should go into work any day this week (we’re technically only allowed to work two days a week from home).
context: Told it may be early labour and to rest, unsure whether to go in to the office.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: A (used to be) close friend of mine since high school disappeared when I got pregnant. Story as old as time.
context: Days before her baby shower, a friend hasn't replied.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote:
Thankfully it eased up around week 13 and I felt amazing and so energized right up until last week. 

I’m now 23 weeks and absolutely exhausted again.
context: Fatigue back at 23 weeks after the second-trimester lift.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I’m currently in bed at mid day after taking a 1 hour lunchtime nap.
context: 23 weeks, exhausted again.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: Immediatley after finding out it felt like a punch to the gut that I wouldn't be able to give him my full attention all the time.
context: Positive test with a 21-month-old at home.

speaker: experienced_mother
quote: I guess I'm looking for input from other parents on the transition to two children, what it's like to have to share your time and attention with two children, age gap advice etc.
context: Under four weeks, second pregnancy.

speaker: new_mother
quote: Thank God I have five months maternity leave which is a blessing. I could NOT do any of this with working.
context: Eight weeks after the birth, overwhelmed by appointments, feeding and housework.

speaker: new_mother
quote: I know people say the dishes can wait but the house being a mess contributes to my anxiety.
context: Eight weeks after the birth, a self-described perfectionist.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: Then, randomly, my job decided to move me when I was 27 weeks. They put me in a unit managing 62 inmates and going up and down stairs frequently. I tried to get them to take me out, but was told there was nothing they could do
context: US corrections worker moved off a desk job late in pregnancy.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: I applied for FMLA, gave it to my doctor's office and let them know that they should fill it out with my last day being June 23rd. I am due July 21st. I'd be 36 weeks at the time and figured this would give me enough time to apply for medicaid. I lose my insurance on my birthday, June 15th, so I had it all worked out.
context: Her dated plan: leave at 36 weeks, insurance ending, Medicaid application.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: With my job, I get 12 weeks of FMLA in a year. 6 weeks unpaid, 6 weeks paid after I have my baby. It worked out. Especially since I plan on giving my job my 2 weeks notice during my last 2 weeks of my maternity leave and not returning.
context: Her understanding of her employer's leave, and her plan not to return.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: They call me back 5 minutes later saying that they can't file early fmla without a valid medical reason.
context: The OB's office on her leave paperwork, due the next day.

speaker: expecting_mother
quote: now I can't take fmla at 36 weeks and have to wait until my due date? I was struggling to understand how I'd manage until June 23rd. But now I have to find out how I'm going to make it to July 21st?!
context: Her leave start may move from 36 weeks to her due date.
